title: Node Object
body:
The node object in JS has a variety of properties
**Key Properties** (important for midterm)
- ID
- NodeName
- TextContent
Insert picture of All node properties taken from phone

---

A single node in the [[DOM]] tree, as opposed to the [[NodeList Object]] that
`querySelectorAll` returns. In practice the ones you handle are [[Element Node]]s.

| Property | Holds |
|---|---|
| `id` | the `id` attribute, or `""` |
| `nodeName` | the tag name, **upper case** (`"LI"`, not `"li"`) |
| `textContent` | all text inside it, descendants included |
| `className` / `classList` | the class attribute, as a string or as a list |
| `style` | inline styles only, not what a stylesheet set |
| `parentNode` / `children` / `firstChild` | the tree links |

The upper-case `nodeName` is the one that costs marks: [[Event Delegation]] checks
`e.target.nodeName == "LI"` and the lower-case version silently never matches.

Setting `textContent` replaces every child with one [[Text Node]]; setting `innerHTML` parses
a string as markup, which is slower and is the [[XSS]] hole. See [[Modifying Documents]].
